message: Sufficient information was found for the Ohio Motion Picture Tax Credit applicable to Cleveland, Ohio. All five sufficiency fields and jurisdiction identity elements are determined.

rounds.objective: Determine whether Cleveland, Ohio (or the jurisdiction it is in) has an active film/TV production incentive programme, and if so, find enough about it to build a cost model: rate, qualifying base definition, caps, payout mechanism, current availability.

findings.evidence_quote: The Ohio Motion Picture Tax Credit provides a refundable tax credit that equals 30% of in-state expenditures (above and below-the-line) on eligible productions.

findings.value_text: Minimum spend of $300,000 in Ohio. Eligible spend includes all production spending and payroll (above-the-line and below-the-line, resident and non-resident) incurred in Ohio.
findings.evidence_quote: Eligible productions must spend a minimum of $300,000 in the State of Ohio

findings.value_text: $50 million annual program cap per fiscal year plus rollover ($5 million set aside for Broadway/theatrical productions); no individual compensation caps.
findings.evidence_quote: Each fiscal year will have a $50 million allocation plus any rollover amounts, with $5 million each year being designated specifically for Broadway/theatrical productions.
At the heart of Ohio film incentives is the Ohio Motion Picture Tax Credit , a 30% refundable tax credit on all qualifying in-state production expenses.

findings.value_text: Active; applications are reviewed and awarded on a rolling basis year-round.
findings.evidence_quote: Applications are reviewed and awarded on a rolling basis year-round.

undetermined_disclosures: Whether this credit is subject to corporation tax was not determined by research; priced as non-taxable. If the real programme is taxable, the true net cash figure would be LOWER than shown here.

Whether an independent audit is mandatory, and any audit fee schedule, was not determined by research; priced with no audit fee deducted. If the real programme requires a paid audit, the true net cash figure would be LOWER than shown here.

Whether an above-the-line per-person compensation ceiling applies was not determined by research; priced with no per-person ceiling. If the real programme caps individual compensation, the true net cash figure would be LOWER than shown here.

When this programme's terms lock (application, start of principal photography, or completion) was not determined by research; assumed at completion for display purposes only — this does not change the computed dollar figure.

The rule model's effective-from date is set to today, the date the programme's current availability was confirmed in force by this research — not the date the programme's rules originally took effect, which was not separately determined.
